newsitem.title: THAILAND: Argentine soymeal to alleviate Thai shortages.
newsitem.headline: Argentine soymeal to alleviate Thai shortages.

text.p: The soymeal supply crunch in Thailand is expected to be alleviated with the arrival of 36,000 tonnes of soymeal from Argentina on Friday, trade sources said.

Vessel Wadi Alkamar, which carried the soymeal, arrived on Friday. The lot was purchased by end-users in early September. The price of the low-protein soymeal was said to be around US$306-307 per tonne c&f Bangkok, they said.
More supply was on the way, trade sources said. Vessel Kavo Kalaikra had left Brazil on October 5 with 54,000 tonnes of soymeal and pellets of Argentine and Brazilian origin.

Vessel Toscana is now loading soymeal at a Brazilian port. The ship will soon sail to Thailand with 27,000 tonnes of Argentine soymeal, 15,000 tonnes of Brazilian soymeal and 8,000 tonnes of sunflower meal.
Additional 37,000 tonnes of soyemal from the two countries were expected to arrive here by mid-November, they said.
On the soybean front, a ship carrying 77,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans was headed for Thailand.
Earlier this week, Thai feedmillers were also said to have bought 12,000 tonnes of soymeal, groundnut meal and rapeseed meal from India for prompt shipment.
The prices were said to be around $308-312 tonne c&f Bangkok.
